title: VSift ocr data v1
description: The data member of a complete or partial ocr result (0.3.0, ADR 0030): what one bounded call read of the on-screen text of a session's video with the optional OCR runner, and how much of the range's plan the session's screen-text index has read. The plan of a range is the representative frame of every visual candidate in it and one frame every coverage.period_us; a call reads at most --max-frames of its pending frames, commits one new index revision, and stops. Run ocr again for the same range to continue: it reads only what is pending. The text itself is found with search, whose first page carries a screen_text member ($defs/search_part) with each hit's frame, time and region. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial with a warning, exactly when coverage.pending or coverage.failed is not 0 or coverage.candidates_complete is false; then its gaps are the candidate_gaps that candidates can still fill, as from-to microsecond ranges, and its reasons name frames_pending, frames_failed and each of those gaps' reasons, once each, in that order. On-screen text is derived, untrusted evidence: quote display_text, and check the frame itself (frame get at the hit's time) before relying on a value.

range.description: The range read: the requested range, or the whole video, clipped to the video.

index.description: The session's newest screen-text index revision after the call; null while no frame of the session has been attempted.

read_now.description: Frames this call attempted: read, or found unreadable.

stopped.description: Why the call ended with frames still pending, or null when it was not stopped. frame_limit: it read --max-frames frames. deadline_exceeded: its time ran out. cancelled: it was cancelled. engine_failed: the OCR runner failed and what it had read before is kept. media_failed: the media tools could not extract a frame. Every stop keeps what was read before it.

candidate_gaps.description: The visual index's gaps in the range, as candidates reports them, in start order. coverage.candidates_complete is false exactly while one of them can still be filled by candidates (not_analyzed, deadline_exceeded); the other reasons are final (their periodic reads are planned as anywhere else). At most 100 are listed.

engine.description: The engine build that read an index: the OCR runner, the ONNX Runtime it loaded and its two models, by version and digest. A different build starts a new index, so text read by two builds is never mixed.

profile.description: ppocrv5-latin-v1: PP-OCRv5 mobile detection with the Latin-script recognizer, read with the runner's fixed settings.

index.description: One immutable revision of the session's screen-text index. A revision holds every frame of the one before it.

frames.description: Frames the index holds, read or unreadable.

lines.description: Lines of text the index holds.

coverage.description: How much of the range's plan the index has read. Every planned frame is counted once: planned = read + failed + unresolved + pending. read: its frame was read (it may hold no text). failed: the runner rejected the image or failed on it; it is not read again by the same build. unresolved: the target time resolved to no decodable frame. pending: not attempted yet. Text that appears and goes between two planned frames is not read.

scope.description: What the block covers: on-screen text only.

period_us.description: The period of the frames planned between candidates: the call's --period-us (default 10000000). In search, the period of the index's latest call; null before ocr has run.

candidates_complete.description: True when no visual window of the range is still to be analysed or tried again (not_analyzed, deadline_exceeded), so the plan holds every candidate the range will have.

reason.description: The visual index's gap reason, as candidates-data.schema.json describes it; run candidates over the range to fill a not_analyzed or deadline_exceeded gap.

frame.description: The exact displayed frame a line was read from, in frame-evidence.schema.json's terms: frame get at time_us returns it.

region.description: The upright rectangle of the frame's displayed pixels the line lies in, inside the frame.

hit.description: One occurrence of the query in on-screen text: a line read on a frame, and how long the same words stayed in the same place over consecutive read frames.

match.description: phrase or all_terms, by the rule search applies to transcript segments.

text.description: The line as the engine read it on the first frame. Hidden characters are kept raw; quote display_text instead.

display_text.description: text with every hidden character written as visible <U+XXXX> notation, as transcript-segment.schema.json defines it.

confidence.description: The engine's own recognition score for the line, provider_uncalibrated: not a probability that the text is right.

last_time_us.description: The time of the last consecutive read frame that held the same words in the same place; equal to frame.time_us when only one did.

frames.description: How many consecutive read frames held it.

candidate_ids.description: The visual candidates whose representative frame the first frame is, in time order; empty for a frame read only for its period. At most 32 are listed.

search_part.description: The screen_text member of a search first page (0.3.0, ADR 0030): the query's occurrences in the session's screen-text index within the searched range, in rank order (phrase matches first, then all-terms matches, each by time), at most the page's limit, with total_hits counting them all. It is on the first page only, never on a page a cursor continues, and it does not change the envelope's status or coverage, which stay the transcript's. state: not_run before ocr has read the session (index is null, every count 0, period_us null and candidates_complete false: nothing about the screen is known); partial while coverage.pending or coverage.failed is not 0 or the candidates are not all known; complete when every planned frame is read or has none. Absence of a hit is never evidence the text was not on screen: only the planned frames were read.
